source_title: Josh Inglis becomes first Australian cricketer to achieve this rare feat in all three formats
source_excerpt: Josh Inglis etched his name into Australian cricket history with a second Test century before Australia were bowled out for 429 on Day 3 of the series-deciding third Test against South Africa at Newlands on Thursday. The visitors secured a crucial 100-run first-innings lead after dismissing the hosts for 329.Inglis scored 102 off 135 balls, including 11 fours and two sixes, to become the first Australian batter to register at least two centuries in each of the three international formats. His landmark knock came on his return to the Test side after nearly a year away from the format and helped Australia build a significant advantage in the series decider.The wicketkeeper-batter reached his century with a reverse sweep against off-spinner Simon Harmer before eventually falling to the same bowler. His innings, combined with Alex Carey's 80, proved instrumental in taking Australia past South Africa's first-innings total.Inglis becomes first Australian with multiple centuries in all three formatsInglis's achievement places him in a unique category in Australian cricket. He now has two centuries each in Tests, ODIs and T20Is, becoming the first Australian batter to reach the milestone across all three formats.His maiden Test century came against Sri Lanka in 2025. He has also registered two ODI hundreds and two T20I centuries, underlining his ability to make an impact across formats.The numbers highlight the significance of his achievement:Tests: 286 runs in six matches, with a highest score of 102, an average of 35.75 and two centuries.ODIs: 1,100 runs in 43 matches, with a highest score of 120 not out, an average of 30.55 and two centuries.T20Is: 1,033 runs in 49 matches, with a highest score of 110, an average of 26.48 and two centuries.Only three Australian batters have scored multiple T20I centuries: Inglis, Glenn Maxwell and Aaron Finch. However, neither Maxwell nor Finch has managed at least two hundreds in all three formats.Maxwell has five T20I centuries and four ODI hundreds, but only one Test ton, scored against India in 2017. Finch, meanwhile, finished his international career with 17 ODI centuries and two T20I hundreds but never scored a Test century.Inglis is now the only Australian batter to have multiple centuries in each format.Inglis makes Test comeback countInglis returned to Australia's playing XI for the series decider after recovering from a fractured finger sustained during the preceding ODI series against South Africa. He had last played a Test during the 2025 Ashes at home.Australia made four changes to their side for the Newlands Test, bringing Inglis back alongside Cameron Green, Nathan Lyon and Cooper Connolly.South Africa had earlier posted 329 in their first innings, putting the onus on Australia's batters to build a substantial response. The visitors crossed that mark through contributions from across the batting order, with Inglis's century and Carey's 80 proving particularly valuable.Australia's innings ended at 429 in 125.1 overs, giving them a 100-run first-innings lead heading into South Africa's second innings.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
